title: oss/v2/buckets/{bucketKey}/objects/batchcompleteupload

responseCodes.col_1: POST https://developer.api.autodesk.com/oss/v2/buckets/{bucketKey}/objects/batchcompleteupload
App only
data:write data:create
JSON
Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a two-legged access token obtained via a Client Credentials Grant flow.
Must be application/json
The bucket key of the bucket that contains the objects you are operating on.
An array of objects, each of which represents an upload to complete.
The URL-encoded human friendly name of the object for which to complete an upload.
The ID uniquely identifying the upload session that was returned when you obtained the signed upload URL.
The expected size of the object. If provided, OSS will check this against the object in S3 and return an error if the size does not match.

An array of eTags. S3 returns an eTag to each upload request, be it for a chunk or an entire file. For a single-part upload, this array contains the expected eTag of the entire object. For a multipart upload, this array contains the expected eTag of each part of the upload; the index of an eTag in the array corresponds to its part number in the upload. If provided, OSS will validate these eTags against the content in S3, and return an error if the eTags do not match.
The Content-Type value for the uploaded object to record within OSS.
The Content-Disposition value for the uploaded object to record within OSS.
The Content-Encoding value for the uploaded object to record within OSS.
The Cache-Control value for the uploaded object to record within OSS.
Custom metadata to be stored with the object, which can be retrieved later on download or when retrieving object details. Must be a JSON object that is less than 100 bytes.
The request was successfully processed. The response body will contain objects that indicate the outcome for each uploaded object.

A map of the returned results; each key in the map corresponds to an object key in the batch, and the value includes the results for that object.
The results returned by the Complete Batch Upload to S3 Signed URLs operation.
If this attribute is not returned, completion has succeeded. If the value of this attribute is “error”, completion failed.’
The bucket key of the bucket the object was uploaded to.
The URL-encoded human friendly name of the object.
An identifier (URN) that uniquely and persistently identifies the object.
The total amount of storage space occupied by the object, in bytes.
The format of the data stored within the object, expressed as a MIME type. This attribute is returned only if it was specified when the object was uploaded.
The Content-Disposition value for the uploaded object as recorded within OSS. This attribute is returned only if it was specified when the object was uploaded.
The Content-Encoding value for the uploaded object as recorded within OSS. This attribute is returned only if it was specified when the object was uploaded.
The Cache-Control value for the uploaded object as recorded within OSS. This attribute is returned only if it was specified when the object was uploaded.
An array containing the status of each part, indicating any issues with eTag or size mismatch issues.
The index of the first part in the multipart upload.

Indicates whether this particular part uploaded to S3 is valid. Possible values are:

Pending - No such part was uploaded to S3 for this index.
Unexpected - The eTag of the part in S3 does not match the one provided in the request.
TooSmall - A chunk uploaded to S3 is smaller than 5MB. Only the final chunk can be smaller than 5MB.
Unexpected+TooSmall - The chunk is both too small and has an eTag mismatch.
Ok - The chunk has no issues.’
The size of the corresponding part detected in S3.
The eTag of the detected part in S3.
The reason for the failure, if the status is error.
